newsitem.title: USA: FCC allows Ameritech to keep Circuit City assets.
newsitem.headline: FCC allows Ameritech to keep Circuit City assets.

text.p: Federal regulators denied a request Tuesday by a security monitoring trade group to force Ameritech Corp. to shed the alarm monitoring business it bought from Circuit City Stores Inc..
The Federal Communications Commission also gave Ameritech the green light to buy the assets of other alarm monitoring businesses in the future.
The Alarm Industry Communications Committee had asked the FCC to force Ameritech to shed the Circuit City assets and to refrain from making similar purchases in the future.

The Chicago-based Baby Bell bought the assets -- including residential and business customer contracts, monitoring center hardware and software, and equipment inventory -- for an undisclosed amount last year.
The committee had cited language in last year's communications law barring Bell phone companies from getting into the alarm monitoring business until after the turn of the century.
But the FCC said Circuit City's "Home Security Division" was not an "alarm monitoring service entity" as spelled out under the new communications law.

Congress had granted Ameritech an exemption because it had gotten into the business in 1994. The carrier can purchase the assets of an alarm monitoring company, but it cannot take an equity stake in a firm.
FCC Commissioner Susan Ness, meanwhile, dissented from the agency's decision, saying she disagreed with her colleague's intrepretation of the law.

In a statement, Ness said the FCC's decision produced an "illogical result:" Ameritech is barred from buying the stock of an alarm monitoring business, "but it may achieve the same result by 'acquiring the assets' of an alarm monitoring service company or division."
